newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal- Rail offers slip on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal- Rail offers slip on weak demand.

text.p: Rail soymeal basis offers slipped on Friday amid a glut of supply and limited demand, several cash brokers said.
"There's certainly no buying interest in the domestic market right now," an Ohio broker said. "Several people have meal on track and it just seems like there's nobody who wants to buy it."

The National Oilseed Processors Association also showed abundant supplies. Thursday's weekly crush figure was within trade expectation but above last year's. NOPA put the crush at 24.54 million bushels, against 24.0 million last year.
Offers slipped $1.00 per ton in Danville, Ill., Lancaster, Penn., and Guntersville, Ala. Offers were down $2.00 per ton in Decatur, Ill.
But some suggested basis levels would rebound soon.
There was widespread market talk that a major U.S. soybean processor planned to cut back production at all of its crushing plants.
Export demand was also said to be quiet. U.S. brokers discounted rumors that China had bought 125,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for July/August delivery, saying Brazilian supplies would be cheaper.
